doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Why she would never take a sabbatical, and musicians who ignore new music
summary: She fears being replaced if she left Piano Jazz, thinks Williams might be a good host, and complains that artists like Teddy Wilson did not know younger players or new tunes.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: We were talking about how does “Piano Jazz,” is “Piano Jazz” so much synonymous with Marian McPartland, that could it exist . . . if you decided to take a

sabbatical or something like that, much like say what Johnny Carson did with “The Tonight Show.” At various times he would do it. At first he was doing it five nights a week. Then he decided, I only want to do it two or three nights, or three or four nights a week and bring in guest hosts. Bill Cosby would do it. Joan Rivers would do it. He had a nucleus of people that was there at various age groups, various . . . or one was a comedian. Sometimes they were involved in other areas. Had you . . . had that occurred to you, that that may be a possibility? For instance you may, your performance schedule might get extremely busy, and you say, “Sherrie, I’m going to take a sabbatical?” What would happen.
Oh, no. Oh, no. I would never do that.
You would never take a sabbatical.
I would never do that. I’d be afraid to do that.

Because . . . you’re in the rat race. I would think to myself, suppose somebody came on, and they thought, maybe we should put Marian on one side and get this guy or female. I just wouldn’t ever take any chances like that.
That’s very kind-hearted of you to say that.

The only way I would do it is if I got sick or . . . Once in a while I do think of who could do it. You’d be a likely candidate. You’re a good interviewer, and you’re not afraid. You’re industrious. You’re not . . . You know so much. You do a lot of research. You know . . . I think a lot of musicians are not interested in other musicians. I remember when I had Teddy on the show, I was surprised at people that were coming up. This is a long time ago, and I can’t remember who I spoke to him about. The people who were coming up that he didn’t know, and tunes that were being played that he didn’t know. I thought, this shouldn’t be. Everyone, everybody should be conversant with what’s happening now. Whether or not you’re going to start playing a Celine Dion tune from The Titanic, at least you should know it exists.
There’s a lot of people that they’re really into their own thing, and they don’t listen that much to . . .
I agree. I think that’s a very sad commentary as well. For instance, would have Teddy Wilson, would have known of McCoy Tyner or Cedar Walton? Would that have been some names at least?
I don’t know. He might have. I don’t recall ever asking him something like that. I know I’m mad at McCoy Tyner. He won’t do another “Piano Jazz.”
